items: In education that prepares children for life. At the heart of our philosophy is a student centric approach: every child has their own skills, values, interests and strengths. We want to unearth these and hone them such that the child can then use these to reach their highest potential.

That there is no substitute for spending time in nature – it is and always will be our greatest and most patient teacher. Our connection with and awareness of our environment deepens with mindful time spent outdoors.

That awareness of the self is one of the essential aims of transformational education. As we become conscious individuals, our love for and acceptance of ourselves, others and the world at large grows.
That compassion is integral to our evolution as a community; our children will engage with kindness and love as a way of life.

In the arts – drama, stories, music, dance, painting – and movement as mediums to teach. Not only do they make learning exciting and fun, they are optimally suited to brain development in pre-schoolers.
pilars: Nature - Neuroscience says that being in nature creates the optimum learning conditions for our brain - multiple parts light up at once. Spending time in nature connects us to our environment and enables a deep reverence for our planet and its wellbeing, which in turn is connected to our own.

Movement - A child's body, especially his brain and limbs, are developing at this age. Fine and gross motor activities form a cornerstone of our approach, bringing a child safely into their physical form and encouraging healthy development of coordination, balance and strength.
Play (self-initiated) - self governed play builds imagination, freedom, and is in essence, a child's 'work'. It allows for optimal development of their brain (working much in the same way as nature).

The Arts - music, dance, storytelling, painting, craft et all, develop the imagination, creativity and expression. The arts are best-suited to the stage of brain development that takes place at this age (before 7yrs). The arts create the rungs in our brain past which left brained activities can then be attempted at a later stage with ease (logic, reasoning, rational thinking).
environment: Our environment is fashioned in a way that is artistically and culturally rich, warm, inviting and innately comfortable to little children.

Children are incredibly sensory at this age and their natural flow involves actively exploring their surroundings with curiosity and openness. Our environment offers limits only with regards safety and protection whilst allowing the children to take risks, learn from experience and engage with challenges.

We focus on real life experiences as opposed to virtual ones such that the child can develop a strong relationship to the real world. However, we do not shut out technology as it is the way of the current generation; we believe in harnessing technology's strengths, remaining in the 'now' (or present) and fully optimising the offerings of the time.

The outdoor space has been left largely to the children's imagination mimicking Forest Kindergartens from Germany. We hope that natural tools such as sticks, stones, mud and leaves form imaginative playthings for children as they learn from and explore the world around them.
